title: Zeus — Echoes in later ages
summary: Zeus, king of the Olympian gods, wields the thunderbolt and upholds justice and hospitality. This study traces the myth's afterlife.
body:
Zeus, king of the Olympian gods, wields the thunderbolt and upholds justice and hospitality. He overthrew his father Cronus after being hidden away by his mother Rhea.

Long after its gods lost worshippers, Zeus kept working — in Renaissance painting, in Romantic poetry, in modern film. Each age found its own anxieties reflected in the old story. Viewed through a narrative lens, Zeus is examined as story — its plot, its pacing, and the moments that make it unforgettable.

Myths survive by being reusable. Zeus proved endlessly reusable. A fourth sub-question examines the moral the myth was meant to teach its first hearers. Related entries in this archive: Maya ballgame and Wendigo.
